name: What is the minimum lot size for a triplex in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How large does a parcel need to be before a triplex becomes feasible in Los Angeles or neighboring cities?
mainEntity.text: How large does a parcel need to be before a triplex becomes feasible in Los Angeles or neighboring cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minimum lot size is not the only or even the best way to judge triplex feasibility. A parcel can be large enough in square footage but still fail due to setbacks, shape, access, parking, or zoning limits. Conversely, a compact lot may support three units if the building is designed efficiently and the code path allows it. The real test is the buildable envelope after all planning and life-safety rules are applied. That is why owners should avoid starting with a generic minimum-lot-size question and instead ask whether the site can accommodate three legal dwelling units with proper access, light, ventilation, and parking. A parcel-specific feasibility analysis is the most reliable answer.
acceptedAnswer.description: There is no single minimum lot size that applies everywhere because triplex feasibility depends on zoning, setbacks, parking, density, and site conditions. A larger lot does not guarantee approval, and a smaller lot may still work with the right configuration. The zoning envelope is more important than raw acreage.
